title: Redesign metrics collection pipeline for inference KPIs (Prometheus + OTel + exemplars)
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Our current metrics pipeline emits a large number of low-value Prometheus metrics from the inference runtime and lacks canonical linkage between traces and metrics. This makes it hard to debug tail-latency spikes, measure batching efficiency, or compute model-level unit economics reliably.

Goal: Replace ad-hoc pushes and mixed exporters with a clear, low-cardinality Prometheus metric surface backed by an OpenTelemetry collector that emits exemplars (trace IDs) for latency histograms, and a recording/aggregation layer (rules) to compute operational KPIs such as tokens_per_second, effective_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_ratio, and p99_token_latency per model. The pipeline should remote_write to Cortex/Thanos for long-term storage and expose a set of Grafana dashboards and alerts.

Scope:
- Instrument serving runtime to emit OTel metrics and resource attributes (model_id, model_variant, deployment_tier) with strict cardinality rules.
- Add histogram buckets appropriate for token generation (microseconds to multiple seconds) and attach exemplars from tracing hooks so Grafana panels can link spikes to trace IDs.
- Deploy OTel Collector (sidecar + central collectors) with batching, retry, and relabel configs; metrics exporter to Prometheus and remote_write to Cortex.
- Create Prometheus recording rules for derived KPIs and Grafana dashboards for latency, errors, batching efficiency, cache hit rate, and cost-per-token.
- Provide migration plan for existing dashboards and a rollback path.

Out of scope: full rework of alerting thresholds across all teams (we will propose defaults but hand-off to SRE).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits OTel metrics for token_latency_histogram, tokens_emitted_total, batch_size_histogram, kv_cache_hit_total with resource attributes model_id, model_variant, deployment_tier
OTel Collector config deployed in staging and prod with relabeling rules to drop high-cardinality labels and ensure low-cardinality model tags
Prometheus histograms include exemplars that contain trace IDs for >=95% of sampled requests above p95 latency
Recording rules compute tokens_per_second, effective_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_ratio per model and are available via Prometheus API

Grafana dashboard (observability/inference/kpis) published with panels for p50/p95/p99 token latency, token throughput, batching efficiency, cache-hit rate, error budget burn; dashboard link added to ticket
End-to-end test demonstrating trace->metric linking: when synthetic workload generates a deliberate tail latency, the Grafana panel provides an exemplar link to the trace in Jaeger/Tempo
Migration plan documented with rollback steps and a runbook for on-call SREs
tasks: RFC: final OTel metric names and labels (constrain cardinality) - draft and review
Add OTel SDK instrumentation to runtime: token events, batching events, cache events
Implement tracing hooks to record exemplar trace_id on histogram observations
OTel Collector: central config, relabel rules, exporter to Prometheus remote_write to Cortex
Create Prometheus recording rules and test in staging
Grafana: build dashboard panels and dashboards provisioning JSON
Create CI job to validate metric cardinality and exemplar presence
Run staged rollout and monitor SLOs; iterate on buckets and labels
